scope: Calibrate the 'AI-native' edge: how AI-heavy practice tools for small firms work in 2025-2026 (Clio's own AI as baseline, Smokeball, MyCase IQ, PracticePanther, LEAP, Filevine, Harvey, Legora, Canadian startups); what the AI does, human review, citations, Canada availability. Research done by web search snippets plus opened pages (lawnext, filevine.com); clio.com and help.clio.com returned 403 and web.archive.org was unreachable, so Clio facts are from search snippets of official pages (medium).
clio_products: Clio Manage (Manage AI, formerly Clio Duo)

features.name: Manage AI deadline extraction from court documents
features.where: Manage AI Launchpad > Schedule events from documents; Calendar > New events > Extract from a document; matter dashboard AI Actions card
features.what: Classifies an uploaded notice/order, extracts dates and drafts calendar events for the user to review; each date shown beside its source text. Help article says it does NOT apply local court day-counting rules.
features.plan_tier: Manage AI add-on / higher tiers (not confirmed)

features.name: Manage AI suggested time entries
features.where: Matter dashboard > AI Action card; AI Launchpad > create time entry
features.what: Proactively suggests unlogged time entries and tasks from matter activity (e.g. completed tasks); user accepts. Also creates entries from a plain-language command.

features.name: Clio Duo / Manage AI in Canada
features.what: Launched in Canada 28 Jul 2025: drafts emails, retrieves matter details, summarizes, suggests time entries. Runs on Azure OpenAI; firm data not used for training; respects user permissions.

features.name: Clio Work agentic mode
features.what: Since Apr 2026, goal-level prompts are decomposed into multi-step tasks run via a 'skills' layer; shows live thinking traces; user can interrupt/redirect mid-task. No pre-execution approval gate described in press.

features.name: Clio Work Canadian data residency
features.what: Data at rest (matters, documents, Vincent conversations) stays in the Canadian region, but generating a response may involve temporary processing outside the region.

features.name: Vincent Canadian case law and legislation
features.what: From 23 Sep 2026 (after Jurisage acquisition) includes 567k+ Canadian decisions and federal/provincial legislation excluding Quebec, with verifiable citations; help tells users to verify via Clio Library sources.

features.name: Smokeball AutoTime (+ AI descriptions)
features.what: Passively records work done in the app (docs, emails, calls) as pending time; AI writes entry descriptions in one click (beta, desktop only); user reviews before billing.

features.name: Smokeball Archie next generation (agentic)
features.what: Jul 2026: multi-step reasoning, visible steps; creates tasks, memos and calendar events with user approval; Word edits as tracked redlines; apps for chronologies, transcription (linked to timestamps), bank-statement analysis (linked to source line); prompt skills, MCP planned. US/AU/UK; no Canada.

features.name: Smokeball AI Intake form builder
features.what: AI builds/digitizes intake forms from existing paperwork; no evidence it turns a completed intake into a matter automatically.

features.name: MyCase IQ
features.what: Summarizes documents (OCR'd PDFs), improves/translates text (EN/ES), suggests first drafts of portal messages, texts and event descriptions; user edits before send. Included at no extra cost. US-focused; no Canadian hosting found.

features.name: PracticePanther AI
features.what: No native AI product found in 2025-2026; latest launch is PantherAccounting Plus (Apr 2026, native trust/operating accounting with bank sync and reconciliation). AI only via third-party integrations.

features.name: LEAP Matter AI
features.what: Answers questions over a matter's docs, emails, scans (OCR, handwriting); cites the documents used with preview; summaries, chronologies, document comparison, 200+ drafting prompts, checks critical dates. Available to all LEAP users including Canada.

features.name: LEAP LawY (lawyer-verified AI answers) and AI Prompts
features.what: LawY answers legal questions by jurisdiction; an answer can be sent to a qualified Canadian lawyer for verification. Launched Ontario first, then BC. AI Prompts tied to Ontario/BC court forms.

features.name: Filevine LOIS + Timely
features.what: LOIS (Oct 2025) routes requests to summarize, extract facts, compute rule-based deadlines, create tasks/appointments; outputs link to case documents for verification. Timely automates jurisdiction-specific deadlines (US). No Canadian hosting found.

features.name: Harvey / Legora
features.what: Research/drafting/review workbenches, not practice management. Harvey reportedly $1k-2k/seat/month with 20-50 seat minimums; Legora $300-800 with ~10-seat minimum. Effectively closed to 1-5 lawyer firms; no Canadian residency info found.

features.name: Canadian AI startups
features.what: Spellbook (NL/Toronto): Word contract drafting, CBA member discount. Alexi (Toronto): litigation research memos. Caseway (Vancouver): AI court-form automation, partnered into MyCase. Jurisage now inside Clio. None is a full AI-native practice-management system for small Ontario firms.

gaps.feature: Passive activity capture for time (Smokeball AutoTime model)
gaps.proposal: Add a passive activity ledger (doc opened/edited, email sent/read, call logged, agent actions) per user per matter with durations; the day-rebuild agent drafts entries from it, each entry linking its source events; AI writes the narrative in firm billing style; user accepts/edits/rejects in one queue.

gaps.feature: Source shown beside each extracted value (Clio deadline extraction, LEAP previews, Filevine links)
gaps.proposal: Keep 'cite to page and line' but render it as a side-by-side highlight of the source span in the document viewer on every review card (deadlines, intake facts, time sources, conflicts hits).

gaps.feature: Accept/reject as tracked changes for drafted documents (Archie in Word)
gaps.proposal: Agent edits to existing documents arrive as tracked redlines with per-change accept/reject and a cited reason; approval queue item is the redline set, not the whole file.

gaps.feature: Mid-task visibility and interrupt (Clio Work thinking traces)
gaps.proposal: Show each running agent job's step list live with stop/redirect; keep our hard approval gate before regulated actions (that remains our differentiator vs Clio Work, which describes interrupt-only control).

gaps.feature: Escalate an AI answer to a human expert (LEAP LawY)
gaps.proposal: 'Ask a colleague to verify' action on any agent answer or memo: routes to a named lawyer in the firm (or opt-in external reviewer) with the question, answer and citations; verdict stored and fed back to evals.

gaps.feature: Matter Q&A and chronology (LEAP Matter AI, Archie apps)
gaps.proposal: Matter screen: ask-the-matter box over docs/emails/scans with cited answers; one-click chronology table (date, event, source cite) exportable to Word.

gaps.feature: Bank-statement analysis linked to source lines (Archie app)
gaps.proposal: Trust matching shows each matched/unmatched transaction linked to its line in the imported statement PDF/CSV; unmatched lines become review items.
Decide link-out vs licence (CanLII API link-out for free; Vincent/Lexis/Westlaw are competitors or costly). Spec: research answers must cite CanLII URLs or firm documents only, never uncited.

gaps.feature: Court-form automation for Ontario (LEAP AI Prompts, Caseway)
gaps.proposal: Agent fills Ontario court forms (e.g. Family Law Rules forms, Rules of Civil Procedure forms) from matter data with each field citing its source; partner (Caseway/DivorceMate) or build a short list first.

corrections.our_claim: Who does the work - Clio: 'People work; AI assists on request'
corrections.truth: Outdated. Clio Work has had an agentic mode since Apr 2026 (goal-level prompts, multi-step execution, skills, no manual trigger), and Manage AI proactively surfaces deadlines and unlogged time on dashboards. The real difference is the control model: Clio describes watch-and-interrupt, we gate regulated steps with approval. Reword to 'Agent can act; control is watching and interrupting' vs ours 'Agent acts; regulated steps wait for sign-off'.

Understated. Clio deadline extraction shows each date beside its source text, and Vincent gives verifiable citations including Canadian case law since Sep 2026. LEAP Matter AI and Filevine LOIS also cite source documents. Our edge is narrower: citation required on every claim, to page and line, enforced (not optional). Say that instead.

corrections.our_claim: Time capture - Clio: 'Timers'; ours: 'Agent rebuilds the day' as unique
corrections.truth: Clio Manage AI already suggests unlogged time entries; Smokeball AutoTime has passively captured activity for years and now writes AI descriptions. Day-rebuild with accept is not unique; claim must be about breadth (email+docs+calendar+agent work) and cited sources per entry, proven in a pilot.

corrections.our_claim: Data - Clio: 'AI may process outside Canada'
corrections.truth: Accurate but incomplete. Clio offers a Canadian region where data at rest (incl. Vincent conversations) stays in Canada; only transient AI processing may leave. State it precisely or it reads as misleading. Our 'all in Canada' must also be true for model inference (Canadian-region model endpoint), otherwise we have the same caveat.

corrections.our_claim: Ontario rules - Clio: 'Mostly US court rules'
corrections.truth: Partly right: Manage AI deadline extraction does not apply local court day-counting rules at all (help article). But LEAP is strong in Ontario (court forms, AI Prompts for ON/BC, LawY launched in Ontario) and Clio now has Ontario case law/legislation via Vincent. 'Ontario rules built in' is an edge over Clio and US tools, not over LEAP for forms.

corrections.our_claim: Deadlines - Clio: 'Entered, or extracted then confirmed'
corrections.truth: Fair. Add the precise point: Clio extracts and shows source but does not compute dates under local court rules; Filevine Timely does compute jurisdiction rules (US only). Our 'rule cited plus blind second check' is a real edge in Ontario if delivered.

Unproven from this research; PracticePanther (Apr 2026) and Clio both offer bank-synced reconciliation tooling. Verify Clio's trust reconciliation workflow (other researcher scope) before claiming 'manual'.

corrections.our_claim: Implied: competitors are not AI-native / approval-first
corrections.truth: Smokeball Archie (Jul 2026) creates tasks/events 'with user approval' and shows Word edits as redlines; MyCase drafts require user edit before send. Approval per action exists elsewhere; our distinct claims are one firm-wide queue, preparer cannot approve own work, and an audit log.

Does Smokeball plan Canada? No evidence found.
